chapters.title: Administration, roles and permissions
intro: This chapter is for administrators. It starts with the **Administration** home, where every setting area begins.
It then explains roles. You learn what each built-in role may do and which records it sees. You also learn how to make your own roles safely.

sections.title: The Administration home
intro: Open **Administration** in the left rail. The page shows one card for each area you can manage, in seven groups.
A card appears when your role holds any of its permissions. Settings you change apply to the next request. Open desks refresh by themselves.

blocks.caption: The **Administration** home with the Organisation and Ticketing groups.
blocks.alt: Administration home with numbered search box, group heading and the Roles and permissions card

callouts: **Find a setting** filters the cards as you type. Press [[Enter]] to open the first match.
A card. Select it to open the area.

sections.title: Administration cards
sections.intro: Some cards open screens outside **Administration**, because supervisors use the same screens. Reading is often allowed more widely than changing.

blocks.note: Hiding a card never replaces a permission check. Each screen checks the permission again when it opens.

sections.title: Built-in roles
sections.intro: Every new workspace gets six system roles. They are read-only. You can clone them to make your own versions.

rows: Agent work plus transfer, bulk changes, delete, approvals, monitoring, costs, team analytics, knowledge review and AI approvals.
Day-to-day ticket work, customers, knowledge drafts, AI help and engineering links.
View tickets and add internal notes.
Knowledge base writing, review, publishing and settings.

blocks.p: The [permission reference](#permission-reference) shows exactly which permissions each role holds.

blocks.caption: The **Roles & permissions** list with six system roles and two custom roles.
blocks.alt: Roles list with numbered New role button, filter box, role name and badges, scope and counts, and actions menu

callouts: **Filter roles** finds a role by name or description.
The role name with badges: **System** or **Custom**, **Administrator** for roles that can manage roles, and **Light agent**.
The ticket scope, the number of permissions and the number of members.
The actions menu: **View** or **Edit**, **Clone** and, for custom roles, **Delete**.

blocks.caption: The actions menu of the custom Account Manager role.
blocks.alt: Roles list with the actions menu open showing Edit, Clone and Delete

blocks.note: Custom roles need a plan that includes them, such as Trial, Professional or Enterprise. On other plans, **New role** and **Clone** are turned off.

sections.title: Data scope
intro: Each role has a ticket scope and a customer scope. They decide which records the role's members can see at all.
A user with several roles gets the broadest scope of them. Records outside the scope are invisible. They behave as if they did not exist.

rows: **Own tickets — assigned to or raised by the agent**
Only customers they manage as account manager.

blocks.caption: The **Data scope** card of the Account Manager role.
blocks.alt: Data scope card with ticket and customer scope options and the Light agent role switch

blocks.note: You cannot give a role a broader scope than your own. Those options are turned off.

sections.title: Open a system role
sections.intro: Select a system role to see its settings. Everything is read-only.

blocks.caption: The Administrator system role, which is read-only.
blocks.alt: Administrator role page with numbered Clone to customise button, read-only notice and General card

callouts: **Clone to customise** makes an editable copy.
The **General** card with the name and description.

sections.title: Clone a role
sections.intro: Cloning is the quickest way to make a role that is close to an existing one.
steps: Open the actions menu of the role and select **Clone**. On a system role page, you can also select **Clone to customise**.

steps.text: In **Name of the new role**, enter a unique name.
steps.caption: The clone panel suggests a name ending in (copy).
steps.alt: Clone Account Manager panel with the Name of the new role field and Clone role button

sections.result: A message says "Role cloned". The new role opens with the same permissions, data scope and light-agent setting.

sections.title: Create a custom role

steps.caption: The **General** card of a new role.
steps.alt: General card with the name Billing desk and a description

steps: In **Data scope**, choose the **Tickets** and **Customers** scopes.
Turn on **Light agent role** only for collaborators who must never reply or own tickets.

steps.text: Under **Permissions**, tick the permissions the role needs.
steps.caption: The permission matrix filtered by the word merge.
steps.alt: Permissions card with numbered filter box, group check box, permission code and Sensitive badge

steps.caption: The save bar shows **Unsaved changes** until you save.
steps.alt: Save bar with Unsaved changes, Discard and Create role

sections.result: A message says "Role created". The **Members** card appears, so you can add people to the role.

blocks.p: The name must be unique and 2–100 characters long. **Discard** throws away your changes.
In the matrix, each permission shows a description and its code. A group check box ticks or clears a whole group. **Sensitive** marks high-impact permissions.

blocks.tip: Type in **Filter permissions** to find a permission by its description or code.

blocks.note: A lock next to a permission means you do not hold it, so you cannot grant it.

sections.title: Add or remove role members
prerequisites: The role is a custom role.

steps.text: In **Members**, choose a user in **Add a user to this role…**.
steps.caption: The **Members** card with one member.
steps.alt: Members card with numbered user picker and Remove button

steps: To take someone out, select **Remove** on their row.
sections.result: A message says "Member added" or "Member removed". The change applies to the member's open sessions at once.

blocks.p: Each member row lists the other roles the person holds. You can also change roles from the agent page. See [Change an agent's roles and departments](#edit-agent-access).

sections.title: Light agents
sections.intro: A light agent is a collaborator who helps on tickets without talking to customers. Engineers and managers are typical light agents.

list: A user is a light agent when their agent record says so. Any light-agent role also makes them one.
Light agents can never reply to customers, own tickets, transfer, bulk-edit or delete. This holds whatever their permissions say.
Light agents count against a separate plan limit. By default it equals the plan's agent limit.
The limit is checked when you invite or reactivate a light agent.

sections.title: The escalation guard
sections.intro: You can never give away more than you have. SupportDesk blocks a change when:

list: you create, change or delete a role with a permission you do not hold;
you create, change or delete a role whose data scope is broader than yours;
you add a user to such a role, or remove a user from it;
you choose such a role as the single sign-on default role;
you create a key or client app for an integration with rights you do not have.

blocks.p: The message names the permissions you lack. Ask an administrator with those permissions to make the change.

blocks.note: This applies to a role's current contents too. You cannot edit a role that already holds permissions you lack.

sections.title: The last-administrator rule
sections.intro: The workspace must always keep at least one administrator. That is an active user with a role that holds `admin.roles`.

blocks.p: SupportDesk refuses any change that would remove the last one:

blocks.tip: Make someone else an administrator first. Then make the change.

sections.title: Delete a custom role
prerequisites: The role is a custom role.
The role is not the single sign-on default role.
steps: Open the actions menu of the role and select **Delete**.

steps.text: If people hold the role, choose a role in **Move members to**.
steps.caption: The delete panel asks where the role's members move.
steps.alt: Delete Account Manager panel with the Move members to list and Delete role button

steps: Select **Delete role**. If nobody holds the role, select **Delete** in the confirmation.
sections.result: A message says "Role deleted". Its members now hold the role you chose.

blocks.warning: You cannot undo a delete. Clone the role first if you might need it again.

blocks.note: System roles cannot be deleted or changed.

sections.title: Permission reference
intro: This table lists every permission, grouped as in the permission matrix. A tick means the built-in role holds it.
**Sensitive** marks high-impact permissions. Light agents lose reply, assign, transfer, delete and bulk rights whatever their roles say.

rows: View tickets within the role's data scope
See support costs and billable amounts. **Sensitive**
Create and edit customers, contacts and locations
Manage products, versions, installations and assets
Manage agent availability, shifts, leave and delegation
Create and link engineering work items
View the engineering board, work items and releases
Create, update and move engineering work items; publish releases
View team, department and organisation analytics
Approve, apply and revert AI-proposed actions. **Sensitive**
Manage departments, teams, brands and calendars
Manage ticket fields, statuses, categories and layouts
Manage email accounts and messaging channels. **Sensitive**
Manage knowledge base settings and portals
Manage AI models, prompts, budgets and agents. **Sensitive**

blocks.p: There are 58 permissions in all. Column headings: Light means Light Agent, and Knowledge means Knowledge Manager.

troubleshooting.cause: Your plan does not include custom roles.
troubleshooting.fix: Upgrade to a plan with custom roles, such as Professional or Enterprise.

troubleshooting.problem: A message says you cannot manage a role because it includes permissions you do not have.
troubleshooting.cause: The escalation guard stops you giving or editing rights you do not hold yourself.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask an administrator who holds those permissions to make the change.

troubleshooting.problem: A message says you cannot manage a role because its data scope is broader than yours.
troubleshooting.cause: The role sees more tickets or customers than you do.
troubleshooting.fix: Ask an administrator with a broader scope to make the change.

troubleshooting.problem: "This change would leave the organisation without an administrator."
troubleshooting.cause: The change removes the last active user who can manage roles.
troubleshooting.fix: Give another user the Administrator role first.

troubleshooting.problem: "System roles cannot be changed. Clone the role to customise it."
troubleshooting.fix: Select **Clone to customise** and edit the copy.

troubleshooting.problem: "Single sign-on gives this role to new users."
troubleshooting.cause: You try to delete the single sign-on default role.
troubleshooting.fix: Choose another default role under **Security & sign-in** > single sign-on first.

troubleshooting.problem: A user still cannot see some tickets after you add a permission.
troubleshooting.cause: The data scope of their roles hides those tickets.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the **Data scope** of the user's roles. The broadest scope across their roles applies.

faq.q: What happens when a user holds two roles?
faq.a: They get every permission of both roles. Their data scope is the broadest scope of the two.

faq.q: Do role changes need the user to sign in again?
faq.a: No. Changes apply to the user's open sessions at once.

faq.q: Can a light agent reply to customers if their role allows it?
faq.a: No. Light agents can never reply, own, transfer, bulk-edit or delete tickets, whatever their permissions say.

faq.q: Why do I not see some cards on the Administration home?
faq.a: A card shows only when your role holds one of its permissions. Ask an administrator if you need another area.

glossary.definition: A role that an administrator creates or clones. You can change its permissions, data scope and members.
The tickets and customers a role's members can see: own, team, departments or all tickets, and account-managed or all customers.
The rule that you cannot grant permissions or a data scope that you do not hold yourself.
One right, such as replying to customers or managing roles. Roles bundle permissions.
A named set of permissions and a data scope that you give to users.
A high-impact permission, such as deleting tickets or managing billing, marked with a Sensitive badge.
One of the six built-in roles. System roles are read-only, but you can clone them.
